title: First Dixieland in Chicago: Bill Johnson and the Ansonia
summary: Bill Johnson's band came first; Elgar brought Perez, Tio and Cottrell from New Orleans to the Ansonia for Mike Fritzel.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Of course, I've heard a lot of those groups too in the last 20, 30 years and so. But when you first came to Chicago, was there any of that type of music here? Is that what you call the Dixieland type? Or did it compare at all?

Oh yes, the original Dixieland outfit had been here. That was the outfit. The first outfit that came from Chicago and played here before the colored Dixieland outfit came here. That was Bill Johnson's outfit.
Now, Bill Johnson's outfit was the first colored Dixieland outfit. I can recall who came here. And they played at 8th Street Theater with Trixie Freganza.
Do you remember about what year that was? I know it's hard to think about exactly the year, but if you can remember about when, in relation maybe to the First World War. Was it before that?
That was around, I would say, in the vicinity of the 15, 1950.

Uh-huh. Just a little before the war. Because just about that time, I went, I was playing at the Washington Theater here, 31st and State. And I sent for Emmanuel Perez, Lorenzo Teal, Louis Cottrell, and I brought an outfit here to work for Mike Fritzel. Yes. At that time, Mike Fritzel had a place on Madison and Paulina. Was that the Ansonia? The Ansonia, that's right. And I put them in the Ansonia for Mike. And I had intended, as the orchestra developed, I had intended to take the move over with me. But they were doing so very well at the Ansonia, and Mike was so very pleased with them that they decided to stay there.
